results.summary:
README now opens on the adopter. Order is: title + one-line pitch → the three-command quickstart in `npx` form (`npx hkb init` / `npx hkb doctor --api` / `npx hkb dispatch --loop 60`) plus three `hkb create`/`list` lines so the first thing a reader sees is a real dependent pair on a board → badges (npm version, CI `test.yml`, node engines, licence) → a ten-line "How it works" (a card is an issue, an edge is a native issue dependency, a lock is a git ref — hence the atomic claim and the free heartbeat, a worker is any harness, the dispatcher is a deterministic tick) → the philosophy bullets, kept verbatim as "What it costs".

Everything else kept its content and moved only in order: Working the board · serve · watch/tail · stats · Harnesses · Actions · MCP · Projects mirror · the Hermes mapping table · Local state · a new Docs section · a one-line requirements/licence footer.

Moved out of the README into the NEW file docs/status.md: the MVP status and the four `hkb doctor --api` observations, each now with the reason it is load-bearing (422-not-409 on a duplicate ref create is the atomic claim; `--force-with-lease` rejecting a moved OR deleted ref is what makes the heartbeat free; `GET git/commits/<sha>` committer date is how a lock ages without a write; the pinned `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10`), plus a "how it is exercised" section on dogfooding and an honest "what is not proven yet" (no second backend, scale untested past tens of tasks, Copilot/Codex have far less mileage than Claude Code).

For #53 and #55: the CI badge points at `.github/workflows/test.yml` (workflow `name: test`) and is live; the npm badge is `https://img.shields.io/npm/v/hkb.svg` and will 404 until the first publish. The README's Docs section lists protocol.md, docs/harnesses.md, docs/status.md, docs/EVALUATION.md — if #53 adds a release/publishing doc, add it there.

NOTE for the rest of the track: PR #56 (node #52) was merged to main and its branch deleted while this node was in flight, so kb/54 was rebased onto main and PR #57 is based on main, not kb/52. main already carries LICENSE + the package metadata. #53 should branch from main too.
